assertions.name: Frobenius moment Gram is PSD (well-posed channel geometry)

description: Operator-selection LP/SDP (prop:operator-selection-lp; lp_dual_solver) over the inter-molecular sub-braid channels {1, σ₁ (H-bond), σ₁² (Hopf link 𝓛_H = T_{2,2}, Vol=0, = van der Waals)} with canonical Markov traces t_i=tr_M(b_i) and Frobenius moment Gram G_{ij}=tr_M(b_i b_j). Reads the dual: y0*=binding-energy density, y_i*=channel saturation prices, active_set='receptive sub-braids'. Answers whether the Hopf/vdW channel σ₁² is a distinct load-bearing channel separate from the directional H-bond σ₁. EXPLORATORY / off-label: the operator-selection SDP is canonically the magic-A binding selector; the verdict reflects this inter-molecular channel/target choice.

data.finding: The operator-selection SDP's verdict on vdW = Hopf link, in two parts. (1) The naive sub-braid basis {1, σ₁, σ₁²} is RANK-DEFICIENT (Gram rank 2, one zero eigenvalue): σ₁² = hσ₁+1 is not independent in H_2(q), so 'vdW = the σ₁² channel' is NOT a separate channel at 2 strands. (2) The independent Wedderburn idempotents ARE the channels: the symmetric block e₊ (trivial rep, q-dim 0.6963) is the Hopf/[2]_q/vdW channel (Vol=0); the antisymmetric block e₋ (q-dim 0.3037) is the directional H-bond channel. The Hopf link decomposes σ₁² = q²·e₊ + q⁻²·e₋ = 60.3% symmetric — i.e. van der Waals IS the symmetric-block (e₊, Vol=0) projection, NOT an algebraically new object. So the framework already CONTAINS vdW as the H_2(q) symmetric block; it is the same [2]_q channel as the Hopf diquark. Exploratory/off-label: the operator-selection SDP is canonically the magic-A binding selector; the channel/target setup is the modelling input.
